items.title: Gold Extends Drop on Stronger-Than-Expected US Employment Data
points: Gold fell after a hot US nonfarm payrolls print added fuel to speculations that the Federal Reserve will seek to raise interest rates to contain inflation.
Bullion slipped as much as 1.5% toward $4,020 an ounce after the report.
Traders also weighed diplomatic efforts to end the Middle East conflict against sharp losses in the artificial intelligence trade that have bruised risk appetite.

The precious metal jumped nearly 4% on Wednesday on the midterm results, as Treasury yields and oil fell on bets that incoming Democrats would push to end the Iran war, and that a divided government would limit further spending and borrowing.
Spot gold fell 0.8% to $4,055.42 an ounce as of 12:40 p.m. in New York, while silver dipped 0.03% to $51.76.
The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index, a gauge of the US currency, was 0.4% higher.

items.title: West Bengal election is not legally valid: Former CEC S.Y. Quraishi
points: Quraishi. | Photo Credit: Shiv Kumar Pushpakar Former Chief Election Commissioner S.Y.
Quraishi alleged that the West Bengal elections were not legally valid.
He reinstated that the decisions at the Election Commission of India should be based on a majority.
“Were the West Bengal elections legally valid?
“This government has been in power for 6-7 months.
But some people are raising questions, maybe because they did not get the outcome that they desired,” Minister Dilip Ghosh said on Friday (November 6, 2026), reacting to Mr. Quraishi’s allegations.

This comes after the former CEC raised allegations against the SIR process and discrepancies at the West Bengal elections while delivering the keynote address at the Hashim Abdul Halim Memorial Lecture on Thursday (November 5, 2026) in Kolkata.

The former CEC said this in reference to The Indian Express report, which had claimed that election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised at least 14 objections to the various decisions allegedly taken unilaterally by CEC Gyanesh Kumar.

items.title: Agasthyamalai conservation case: SC directs temporary and non-resident silk cotton cultivators not eligible for protection under FRA Act
points: The Supreme Court directed on Friday that individuals with temporary residence in the Agasthyamalai biosphere or those living entirely outside the forest boundaries cannot be classified as traditional forest dwellers merely for cultivating silk cotton…

According to Tamil Nadu’s own affidavit, 232 persons are cultivating the forest area with temporary residence while 2,767 persons who occupy 2,867.70 hectares land are residing outside the forest boundary and are managing silk cotton cultivation.

The order was passed in furtherance of a May 2026 judgment, which had issued various directions for a structured and time-bound process of eviction, rehabilitation and ecological restoration in the forest areas.
Justice Mehta, who authored the order, held the State government “primarily responsible” for delaying the receipt of claims under the 2006 Act.
Gavai to supervise the expeditious disposal of claims and scrutinise the orders passed by the competent authorities under the 2006 Act.
Presently, 3,637.83.2 hectares of the 5,072.64.3 hectares of forest land is under silk cotton cultivation.

items.title: Supreme Court decision on BBMB arrears a victory for Himachal, says CM Sukhu
points: The order settles a decades-old dispute over Himachal Pradesh’s 7.19% share in the power generated from the projects.

The State will receive nearly 60 crore units annually during the lean season, generating an estimated revenue of ₹10,000 crore to ₹20,000 crore over the 20-year period, depending on electricity prices, Mr. Sukhu said in a statement.
He said the decision could fetch the State additional revenue of up to ₹1,000 crore annually.
Even at ₹6 per unit, Himachal Pradesh would earn at least ₹500 crore a year, while a rate of ₹13-14 per unit would significantly increase the returns.
Mr. Sukhu attributed the outcome to the State government’s sustained legal battle and determination to secure its financial rights.
He described it as the fourth major success in protecting Himachal Pradesh’s interests, citing earlier victories in matters relating to Wildflower Hall, the Kishau Dam among others.
The Chief Minister said the government was also pursuing its claims over the Shanan Power Project and the water cess.

items.title: Quick Mart IPO Draws Strong Demand as Kenyan Listings Pick Up
points: (Bloomberg) -- Quick Mart Plc saw demand for shares in its initial public offering exceed the number available by almost 23% as Kenya’s second-biggest supermarket chain concluded the nation’s second IPO of the year.
Investors applied for 2.45 billion shares at 7.50 shillings each in the Nairobi-based company while 2 billion were on offer, it said in a statement on Friday.
“The board is delighted with the strong response,” Quick Mart said.
Quick Mart is only the second company to pursue an IPO this year in Nairobi after state-run Kenya Pipeline Co. ’s offer.

Rising share prices have helped to create a more favorable backdrop for investors, with the nation’s benchmark stocks gauge gaining 28% in dollar terms this year, placing it among the 10 best performers globally.

Just over 18,000 Kenyan and East African retail investors received a full allocation of 119.6 million shares, while 44 foreign buyers got about 236 million shares, or just under half the number sought.

items.title: Did all the murders happen in the small house on the terrace?
points: Reaching the second floor itself through a very narrow staircase itself is a task.
The building has commercial establishments on the ground floor, including a watch repair shop, a tea stall and a small condiments shop.
The entire first floor was occupied by a small political party.
Indushekar’s house is on the second floor, which also serves as the terrace.
Household appliances were crammed into the space, with several other household items scattered around.
A board on the wall read, “Police Voice”.
This has raised questions as to whether all seven murders were committed here in the house.
However, the accused claimed that the murders took place inside his house.

items.title: Bamboo shelters, cool roofs to climate-proof Telangana cities
points: The measures, backed by new urban policies and a project pipeline worth about ₹20,000 crore, are part of the State’s long-term Telangana Rising 2047 vision.
Of the 43 projects proposed under the Urban Challenge Fund (UCF), three have secured approval.
The bio-mining programme has helped avoid an estimated 5.6 lakh tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions and reclaimed about 418 acres for productive urban use, Ms. Sreedevi said.

Dedicated Climate Change Cells, city-specific action plans and nine Climate Action Officers are also planned for municipal corporations outside Hyderabad: Greater Warangal, Karimnagar, Khammam, Nizamabad, Ramagundam, Nalgonda, Mancherial, Mahabubnagar and…
A key intervention is the Cool Roof Policy, effective from April 1, 2023, to March 31, 2028.
It targets 300 sq km of cool roofs, including 200 sq km in the Hyderabad metropolitan region and 100 sq km in other urban local bodies.
Cool roofs reflect about 80% of incoming sunlight, against 20% for conventional roofs.

items.title: Karnataka CM ridicules BJP leaders for trying to take credit for PM’s visit
points: Shivakumar on Friday alleged that some BJP leaders were trying to take credit for Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Bengaluru on November 13 to inaugurate the metro Pink Line, even though he was arriving on the official invitation of the State…

Without taking the name of BJP MP Tejasvi Surya, the Chief Minister alleged that some BJP leaders were trying to take publicity by claiming that they were responsible for the Prime Minsiter’s proposed visit.
Speaking to media persons in Kanakapura, he wondered why the BJP leaders were tying to take publicity for this event though they had nothing to do with it.
“We are developing metro network by borrowing money.
I will present some of these issues before the Prime Minister on November 13,” he said.

items.title: Governor asks for status report on all public universities in Karnataka
points: Sudha Yadav, Governor of Karnataka and Chancellor of universities in the State, directed all public universities in the State to conduct a comprehensive review of their current operations and identify areas requiring improvement.
The Governor instructed all Vice-Chancellors to prepare and submit a detailed report on the same.
“This report should cover the current status of their respective universities, key achievements, challenges, shortcomings, and specific measures proposed for improvement,” she stated.

Addressing the Vice-Chancellors of various universities and officials from the Karnataka State Higher Education Council at Lok Bhavan, the Governor emphasised the need to strengthen the quality, transparency, accountability and overall performance of…

“Emphasis must be placed on the effective implementation of the National Education Policy and the State Education Policy, strong coordination between industries and universities, as well as skill development, research, innovation and employability,” she said.
The Governor called upon all Vice-Chancellors and the Karnataka State Higher Education Council to work in coordination and collaboration to strengthen the higher education system in Karnataka.

items.title: Periyar Arivulagam books row: political leaders raise concern over allegations, call for action
points: Rajya Sabha Member Kamal Haasan. | Photo Credit: B.

In a statement, he said the reputation of Tamil language would be irreparably damaged if people read, took notes, and incorporated the contents of (fabricated books) into speeches, written works, and research.

VELANKANNI RAJ He said: “It has come to light that 1,800 books published under the name of a publishing house called Akalvilakku Publications have been procured and placed on the library’s fourth floor.
JOTHI RAMALINGAM He added that all the books kept in Periyar Arivulagam should be audited and fabricated books should be removed.
“School Education Minister Rajmohan has seconded these allegations,” he said.

Dr. Anbumani added: “I urge the government to order an investigation by the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption into the alleged corruption in the procurement of books for the Periyar Arivulagam.” We The Leaders founder K.
Annamalai on Friday called for an investigation into allegations of irregularities in the procurement of books for Periyar Arivulagam.

items.title: Special Public Prosecutors appointed to conduct trial in POCSO Act cases against Veeramani
points: The Tamil Nadu government has appointed three Special Public Prosecutors to conduct the trial in the cases booked against Gem Granites owner R.
Veeramani under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012.
In an order issued on Friday, the State Government said considering the sensitive and complex nature of the cases, K.R.
Sandhiya and Swami Subramanian were appointed as Special Public Prosecutors under Section 31(1) of the Act to conduct prosecution of the case investigated by the Special Investigation Team (SIT).
Mr Veeramani and his associates are facing seven cases under the POCSO Act and one case of abetment to suicide of a minor in 2004.
Police sources said that the investigation in at least two cases was in the final stages of completion and chargesheets were likely to be filed next week.

items.title: T.N. govt. allocates monthly maintenance fund of ₹1,000 to 12,646 VAO offices
points: The Tamil Nadu government has issued an order allocating ₹1,000 each as a monthly maintenance fund to 12,646 Village Administrative Officer (VAO) offices functioning across the State, involving an annual expenditure of ₹15.18 crore.
A Government Order to this effect was issued by the Revenue and Disaster Management Department on Friday.
It follows an announcement made by Minister for Revenue and Disaster Management K.A.
Sengottaiyan in the Assembly on August 17 during the Budget session.
The monthly maintenance fund will be credited to the VAOs’ salaries under the head of maintenance allowance.
The government has also allocated ₹8.85 crore towards this fund for the period from September 2026 to March 2027 in the current financial year.

items.title: University of Madras, Sutherland Global Services to collaborate for setting up an AI lab
points: The Syndicate of University of Madras (UoM) on Friday approved a proposal to sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Sutherland Global Services, a digital-driven business transformation company, to set up an AI laboratory at the Department of Women…
The company has offered to upgrade its older allocation of ₹50 lakh for a Gender Lab that was set up at the Department following an older MoU signed in April 2019.
The lab offered an online course on Gender Sensitisation and Workplace Readiness to students across the four campuses of the University.

In addition to reviving the Gender Lab, the MoU seeks to establish an Artificial Intelligence Lab for Inclusive Education that would develop e-modules for a course on Application of Artificial Intelligence.

The Syndicate also cleared a few long-pending issues that have been holding up recruitment of faculty members to various Arts and Science self-financing colleges and government-aided colleges (self financing courses).

items.title: T.N. govt. enhances compensation for various categories of human-wildlife conflict
points: The Tamil Nadu government has enhanced the rates of compensation for various categories of human-wildlife conflict occurring inside and outside protected areas and reserved forests.

According to the order, the compensation for major injuries or partial disability resulting in 20% to 60% incapacitation for humans, duly certified by the District Medical Officer or a constituted medical board, has been increased from ₹59,100 to a maximum…
For minor injuries, the compensation, which was not provided earlier, has now been fixed at a maximum of ₹20,000.

For crop damage, the earlier compensation of ₹25,000 per acre or the actual loss, whichever was less, has been increased to ₹40,000 per acre or the proportionate amount based on the actual damaged area assessed, whichever is less.
The compensation for damage to coconut trees has also been revised from the earlier flat rate of ₹500 per tree.
Earlier, the compensation was ₹10,000 for a fully damaged kutcha house and ₹5,000 for a severely damaged one.

items.title: Rajnath Singh to celebrate Deepavali with troops at India-China border in Sikkim
points: File picture of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh interacting with troops during a visit to Siachen Base Camp, in Ladakh.

Image for representation | Photo Credit: PTI Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will celebrate Deepavali with Army personnel deployed along the India-China border at Nathu La in Sikkim, a senior Defence Ministry official said on Friday.
Mr. Singh will be in Sikkim on Saturday and Sunday and will celebrate the festival with troops guarding the border.
The Defence Minister has made it a tradition to celebrate Vijayadashami (Dussehra) with frontline troops at key military stations across the country.
His visit to Nathu La comes amid continued efforts by India and China to maintain peace along the Line of Actual Control (LAC).
In September, the Indian and Chinese armies held their first Corps Commander-level meeting in the Eastern Sector, marking an expansion of the military dialogue mechanism beyond the Ladakh sector.

items.title: Duraimurugan clarifies on Hindu rituals at granddaughter’s wedding
points: Under fire from the Dravidar Kazhagam and its affiliates for conducting his granddaughter’s wedding with traditional Hindi rituals recently, DMK general secretary Duraimurugan on Friday said it was done as per her wishes.

Clarifying his stance amid the backlash, Mr Duraimurugan in a statement said: “My granddaughter, educated overseas, shared with me that she was in love with an individual outside our caste and wished to marry him with traditional Hindu rituals.
The ceremony was held entirely at her request.
I conceded to the arrangement only due to her strong persistence.
I express my regret over this development and request everyone not to make it a political issue or a subject of debate”.

items.title: AIDSO protests in Kalaburagi and Ballari against proposed closure of 45,000 government schools
points: The protests were held at Thimmapur Circle in Kalaburagi and OPD Circle in Ballari.

The demonstrators condemned the Congress government for allegedly moving ahead with the policy despite strong public opposition and demanded that it withdraw the proposal and protect the public education system.

Addressing the protesters in Kalaburagi, AIDSO district president Tuljaram N.K. alleged that the government, which had promised to protect government schools before coming to power, was now preparing to close thousands of them in the name of the KPS Magnet…
He claimed that the conditions mentioned in the loan agreement with the Asian Development Bank (ADB) clearly indicated the proposed changes.
They also claimed that future teacher recruitment would be restricted to KPS schools and that the government would stop providing grants to these schools after 2030.
The protesters expressed concern that the policy would leave only 4,038 schools functioning in Karnataka while resulting in the closure of around 45,000 government schools.

items.title: Adani Ports Makes Major Push Into Europe With $2.9 Billion Evos Acquisition
points: Adani Ports has agreed to acquire Evos in a €2.56 billion deal.

(Photo: Evos via Port of Hamburg) India’s Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone (APSEZ) has agreed to acquire Netherlands-based liquid storage operator Evos B.V. in a €2.56 billion ($2.88 billion) deal that will give the company a major foothold in…
The agreement, announced Thursday, will see Adani acquire 100% of Evos from Igneo Infrastructure Partners.
Evos is Europe’s second-largest independent liquid storage operator, with eight port-based terminals across the Netherlands, Germany, Spain, Belgium and Malta.

“Evos marks an important milestone in APSEZ’s trajectory towards handling 1 billion tons of cargo and building a truly global, integrated transport platform,” said Karan Adani, managing director of APSEZ.
Adani said the business has maintained average commercial occupancy of 99%, with much of its revenue supported by long-term contracts.

items.title: Delhi College Accountant Duped Of Rs 80 Lakh In 'Boss Fraud'
points: A college accountant in Delhi was tricked into transferring Rs 80 lakh from the institution's bank account by a scamster impersonating a senior official of the institute.

However, the Delhi Police's cyber crime unit, Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations (IFSO), not only arrested the key suspect but also managed to freeze and recover 100% of the defrauded amount within 48 hours.
The incident happened in Delhi's Chanderprabhu Jain College of Higher Studies and School of Law located in Narela, run by Rishi Aurobindo Educational Society.
On October 27, 2026, the society's General Secretary, Abhishek Jain, lodged an e-FIR with the Special Cell's IFSO unit after discovering the fraud.
2 Injured, Several Cars Damaged According to the complaint, an unknown person, using the identity of a senior official of the institution, contacted the college accountant on WhatsApp.

items.title: CLARKSONS HELLAS – SnP WEEKLY
points: The main discussion over the past few months has consistently been the significant increase in Hormuz crude oil flows and the associated surge in tanker earnings.
Following the onset of the US-Iran crisis, cargo volumes shipped from the MEG to the East initially remained relatively modest amid the threats posed.
However, shuttle volumes through the strait subsequently increased significantly, reaching an estimated average of 10.5 mb/d in October.
This provided a small subset of the tanker fleet with the opportunity to become considerably more productive, as vessels only needed to carry cargoes over short distances for ship-to-ship transfers.

Today, after a largely uninterrupted 6-month-rally of upward Tanker momentum, and in the wake of the Democrats’ election victory, we are noticing a drop in tanker equity valuations reflecting a substantial decline in freight rates.

On a more positive note, however, demand for Panamax vessels from Far Eastern buyers stands out as particularly strong while geared tonnage remains in high demand across both basins, as reflected in firm earnings and asset prices.
